headline: Natural Gas Surges as European Supplies Face Severe Winter Risk Concerns
paragraphs: Natural gas skyrocketed 17.79 percent on the day, building on a 9.86 percent weekly gain, as prices in Europe reached a four-year high on persistent winter risks and supply anxiety. Brent crude dropped 4.59 percent, retreating as markets pinned hopes on Middle East diplomacy. The euro traded at 1.1130 against the dollar, providing a stable conversion rate for Irish businesses as local fuel and heating costs react to these volatile energy swings.

Precious metals and other energy commodities saw mixed movement ahead of the impending Federal Reserve rate decision. Gold rose 0.94 percent to EUR 3662.56 per ounce, holding critical support as the market watches the Fed, though analysts note that a strong dollar and high yields continue to weigh on its broader outlook. Silver and platinum dropped over five and four percent respectively on a weekly basis, hitting year-to-date lows as a strong US dollar broke out. Meanwhile, palladium slipped 0.94 percent on the day and over fourteen percent for the month, following UBS downgrades citing weaker investor sentiment and declining Chinese imports.
